I am starting a new research project. The first step is to understand the baseline performance and the existing "working recipe." The training was performed on 10 tickers that are sector-matched with the evaluation set.

The current weight decay of 0.01 is a standard default, but it may not be the optimal value for this specific finetuning task. I hypothesize that increasing the weight decay will introduce stronger regularization, which could help prevent the model from overfitting to the 10 training tickers and improve its generalization to the held-out evaluation set. A stronger regularization penalty will encourage smaller model weights, potentially leading to a simpler and more robust model.

I will test this by doubling the weight decay to 0.02.
